status_summary: Congress enacted the DPC and HSA changes in Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04), and the IRS explained them in Notice 2026-5, released with IR-2025-119 on 2025-12-09. Beginning 2026-01-01 (months after 2025-12-31), a qualifying DPC arrangement (primary care only, fixed periodic fee up to $150 a month per person or $300 for more than one person) does not disqualify a person from contributing to an HSA, and HSA funds can pay its fees; bronze and catastrophic marketplace plans are treated as HSA-compatible high-deductible plans; and the telehealth safe harbor became permanent. Rev. Proc. 2026-24 (Internal Revenue Bulletin of 2026-06-15) states the DPC fee limits for months beginning in 2027 as $150 and $300 and cites section 71308 of Public Law 119-21. This record does not cover the same section's recommendations on short-term plans, association health plans and individual coverage HRAs; Federal Register queries found no rule or proposal on short-term plans or association health plans since 2025-01-20.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; sections 71306 to 71308 make the telehealth safe harbor for high-deductible plans permanent, treat bronze and catastrophic marketplace plans as HSA-compatible, and provide that qualifying direct primary care arrangements do not bar HSA contributions.

The IRS releases Notice 2026-5 (Expanded Availability of Health Savings Accounts under the One, Big, Beautiful Bill Act), explaining the DPC rules (primary care services only, fixed periodic fee capped at $150 a month per individual or $300 for several people), the bronze and catastrophic plan rule, and the permanent telehealth safe harbor; comments requested by 2026-03-06.

The direct primary care and bronze or catastrophic plan HSA provisions take effect for months beginning after 2025-12-31 (the IRS states 2026-01-01); the telehealth safe harbor applies to plan years beginning on or after 2025-01-01.

The IRS publishes Rev. Proc. 2026-24 in Internal Revenue Bulletin 2026-25: it sets the 2027 HSA contribution and high-deductible plan limits and states the direct primary care fee limits for months beginning in 2027 as $150 a month per individual and $300 where the arrangement covers more than one person, citing section 71308 of Public Law 119-21 (Internal Revenue Code section 223(c)(1)(E)) as the source of the provision.

title: Clarify that direct primary care fees do not bar HSA eligibility and expand HSA access
uncertainties: The statute text of Public Law 119-21 was not read; the section numbers and effects come from IRS Notice 2026-5 and Rev. Proc. 2026-24, and the 2025-12-09 release date comes from IRS release IR-2025-119, which announces the notice. Whether a record limited to the HSA and DPC items should be 'completed' rather than 'implemented' is a judgment call: the DPC clarification matches the Mandate in principle but with a fee cap and scope limits, and the broader 'expanded access' call is open-ended. Federal Register queries run since 2025-01-20: 'short-term limited-duration insurance' (only price transparency and marketplace rules), 'association health plans' (only the Marketplace Integrity rule and unrelated items) and 'individual coverage health reimbursement' (only the marketplace payment notices); these show no short-term plan or association health plan rulemaking, but non-Federal Register guidance (for example enforcement statements) was not searched. No news search was run on this objective beyond the IRS notice date. Checks on 2026-10-14: a Federal Register search for 'direct primary care' from 2026-01-01 returned no documents; a web search for later IRS guidance found Rev. Proc. 2026-24 and nothing that delays or narrows the provision. The statute text was still not read directly (congress.gov blocked automated fetch); section 71308 as the direct primary care provision comes from the text of Rev. Proc. 2026-24. Rev. Proc. 2026-24 states no separate release date, so the bulletin issue date is used. Reviewer check 2026-10-14: IR-2025-119 confirms the DPC provision applies from 2026-01-01 and that HSA funds may pay periodic DPC fees (it does not state the fee cap or scope); Rev. Proc. 2026-24 states $150 and $300 as the 2027 DPC fee limits, ties them to section 71308 and gives no issue date. HHS's 2027 payment notice (published 2026-05-20) was removed from this record: its Federal Register abstract addresses catastrophic and bronze plan cost sharing and other Exchange rules but does not mention HSAs or direct primary care, so it is not an action on this recommendation.
